title: From Hormuz to the Caucasus: The New Geography of Energy Security
gist: Aidin Panahi argues that Western energy security now runs on two parallel geographies: the irreplaceable Strait of Hormuz and a slower-building network of Caspian and South Caucasus overland corridors. The corridors add only marginal redundancy for Europe and cannot touch Hormuz's Asia-bound volumes, but they reprice Iran's geography downward while making Turkey the near-indispensable transit state.

insights.claim: About 20 million barrels of oil a day crossed the Strait of Hormuz in 2024, roughly a fifth of global petroleum-liquids consumption, along with about one-fifth of the world's traded LNG, most of it from Qatar.
insights.speaker: Aidin Panahi
insights.so_what: Quantifies the single-chokepoint exposure that drives oil-price and insurance repricing whenever the Gulf destabilizes.
insights.quote: About 20 million barrels of oil a day crossed Hormuz in 2024, roughly a fifth of global petroleum-liquids consumption
insights.locator: The scale of that leverage was on display this year

insights.claim: During the 2026 U.S.-Iran confrontation, oil flows through Hormuz fell to about 4.9 million barrels a day in Q2 2026 from 21.6 million two quarters earlier, with LNG shipments all but ceasing, per EIA estimates that it cautions rest on unreliable vessel-tracking data since February.
insights.speaker: Aidin Panahi
insights.so_what: A ~77% collapse in strait flows during the confrontation shows the tail risk that a Gulf crisis prices into oil and shipping.
insights.quote: oil flows through the strait fell to about 4.9 million barrels a day in the second quarter of 2026, from 21.6 million two quarters earlier
insights.locator: Then, during the confrontation between the United States and Iran

insights.claim: In 2024, 84% of the crude and 83% of the LNG crossing Hormuz went to Asia, mostly to China, India, Japan, and South Korea, so no Caucasus overland route can hedge that exposure because none touches the Asia-bound volumes.
insights.speaker: Aidin Panahi
insights.so_what: Establishes that corridor diversification protects Europe, not Asia, so Asian buyers remain structurally exposed to Hormuz.
insights.quote: In 2024, 84 percent of the crude and 83 percent of the liquefied natural gas crossing Hormuz went to Asia
insights.locator: No overland route through the Caucasus

insights.claim: Panahi frames Hormuz as simultaneously irreplaceable and able to choke the global system at will, arguing new corridors add redundancy for Europe but do not diminish the strait's central role.
insights.speaker: Aidin Panahi
insights.so_what: The paradox means corridor buildout will not lower the geopolitical risk premium tied to the Gulf.
insights.quote: The strait is at once irreplaceable and, as the spring showed, able to choke the system at will.
insights.locator: That is the paradox driving the corridor race

insights.claim: The Baku-Tbilisi-Ceyhan pipeline, valued for crossing Georgia to Turkey without touching Russian or Iranian soil, moved about 206 million barrels in 2025 (roughly 565,000 a day), under half its 1.2 million-barrel-a-day nameplate capacity and down almost 8% on the year.
insights.speaker: Aidin Panahi
insights.so_what: Shows the flagship non-Russian, non-Iranian route is politically significant but volumetrically marginal and declining.
insights.quote: the line moved about 206 million barrels in 2025 — roughly 565,000 a day — under half its rated capacity and down almost 8 percent on the year
insights.locator: The Baku-Tbilisi-Ceyhan pipeline carries Caspian crude

insights.claim: Azerbaijani gas reached Europe via the Southern Gas Corridor at about 12.8 billion cubic meters in 2025, tiny against the EU's roughly 335 billion cubic meters of annual demand, and the cited 31-bcm Trans-Anatolian expansion ceiling is unfunded engineering headroom, not a committed plan.
insights.speaker: Aidin Panahi
insights.so_what: Caspian gas cannot materially replace Russian or Gulf supply for Europe at current or funded volumes.
insights.quote: The frequently cited ceiling of expanding the Trans-Anatolian line to 31 billion cubic meters is engineering headroom, not a funded plan
insights.locator: When it comes to natural gas, the story is similar

insights.claim: The proposed Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity across southern Armenia, linking Azerbaijan to its Nakhchivan exclave and onward to Turkey, is still only a framework whose underlying settlement was initialed at the White House in August 2025 but remains unsigned, with Baku conditioning signature on Armenian constitutional change.
insights.speaker: Aidin Panahi
entities: Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity
insights.so_what: A headline corridor remains contingent on an unsigned settlement, so its option value should not be priced as if operational.
insights.quote: the settlement it depends on was only initialed at the White House in August 2025 and remains unsigned
insights.locator: Some might point to the Trump Route

insights.claim: The Trump Route's proposed structure would give a U.S.-majority company (74% American, 26% Armenian) development rights for an initial 49 years while Armenia retains border, customs, tax, and security authority, displacing Russia's 2020-ceasefire border-guard role without transferring Armenian sovereignty.
insights.speaker: Aidin Panahi
entities: Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity
insights.so_what: The design is a concrete redistribution of influence away from Russia, a geopolitical marker more meaningful than its volumes.
insights.quote: A U.S.-majority company would hold development rights for an initial 49 years — 74 percent American and 26 percent Armenian
insights.locator: A U.S.-majority company would hold development rights

insights.claim: Because most westbound Caspian routes (Baku-Tbilisi-Ceyhan, the Southern Gas Corridor, the Middle Corridor, and the proposed southern Armenia route) either cross Turkish territory or terminate at a Turkish port, Turkey becomes the near-indispensable transit state and an independent broker able to set its own terms against Europe, Washington, Moscow, and Tehran.
insights.speaker: Aidin Panahi
insights.so_what: The more the corridor strategy succeeds, the more leverage accrues to Ankara, a key variable for anyone betting on Caspian energy routing.
insights.quote: which makes Ankara the near-indispensable transit state for Caspian energy moving west
insights.locator: If any state gains from this rearrangement, it is Turkey

insights.claim: Panahi argues land corridors are harder to defend than a maritime chokepoint because they stretch across thousands of kilometers of fixed, largely undefended infrastructure and multiple jurisdictions within reach of Russian and Iranian standoff weapons, so diversification spreads risk rather than eliminating it.
insights.speaker: Aidin Panahi
insights.so_what: Corridor diversification trades concentration risk for a wider attack surface, keeping physical-disruption risk material.
insights.quote: Land corridors present a different problem, stretching across thousands of kilometers of fixed, largely undefended infrastructure
insights.locator: A maritime chokepoint is a concentrated theater

insights.claim: In July 2026 drone strikes on the Black Sea terminal of the Caspian Pipeline Consortium cut loadings by more than a fifth, several hundred thousand barrels a day, on a route that carries close to 2% of world oil supply and is Kazakhstan's main outlet to the sea.
insights.speaker: Aidin Panahi
insights.so_what: A concrete recent strike shows overland/coastal routes are already being disrupted, a supply risk for Kazakh crude.
insights.quote: drone strikes on the Black Sea terminal of the Caspian Pipeline Consortium cut loadings by more than a fifth

insights.claim: Pipeline segments in Azerbaijan, Georgia, and Armenia lie outside NATO territory, so sabotage against them would not automatically invoke NATO's mutual-defense clause, echoing the unattributed 2022 Nord Stream sabotage.
insights.speaker: Aidin Panahi
insights.so_what: The absence of an Article 5 backstop leaves these corridors exposed to deniable attack with limited recourse.
insights.quote: sabotage against them would not automatically invoke its mutual defense clause
insights.locator: Pipeline segments in Azerbaijan, Georgia, and Armenia

insights.claim: Panahi argues Iran is not being bypassed so much as excluded from Western and Gulf-Arab corridors while being hard-wired into the Russia-centered International North-South Transport Corridor, whose missing Rasht-Astara railway link reached a financing agreement in early 2026 as corridor trade roughly doubled in 2024.
insights.speaker: Aidin Panahi
insights.so_what: Iran's integration into the Russian network is adverse lock-in, making it a captive, sanctions-shadowed, lower-value node.
insights.quote: Iran is excluded from the Western and Persian Gulf-Arab corridor systems while being hard-wired into the competing Russian-centered one

insights.claim: Iran's 25-year partnership with China has produced discounted oil sales but little of the promised investment, thinning its eastern hedge.
insights.speaker: Aidin Panahi
insights.so_what: Undercuts the assumption that China provides Iran a robust economic alternative to Western integration.
insights.quote: The 25-year partnership with China has produced discounted oil sales but little of the promised investment.

insights.claim: Panahi argues Iran is trading the profitable position of a country the world wants to route through for the impoverished position of a chokepoint the world spends billions to route around, retaining only the self-diminishing leverage to raise costs and insurance premiums by threatening Hormuz.
insights.speaker: Aidin Panahi
insights.so_what: Frames the corridor race as a structural downgrade of Iran's economic geography, a long-run bearish signal for its transit relevance.
insights.quote: trading the profitable position of a country the world wants to route through for the impoverished position of a chokepoint the world spends billions to route around
insights.locator: The leverage Iran keeps is of a specific, self-diminishing kind

insights.claim: Panahi concludes that diversification is only a partial strategy: it reprices Iran's geography downward by building a competing Eurasian transit network, but leaves the underlying dependence on Hormuz, concentrated in Asia, largely unchanged.
insights.speaker: Aidin Panahi
insights.so_what: The bottom line for markets: corridors erode Iran's position but do not remove the Hormuz risk premium that moves oil.
insights.quote: That lowers the premium on Iran’s position while leaving the underlying dependence on Hormuz largely unchanged.
insights.locator: On that measure, diversification is a partial strategy
